lines.text: Lesson eight: stop-loss and take-profit.
lines.say: Lesson eight: stop-loss and take-profit.

lines.text: Plan your exit before you enter.
lines.say: Plan your exit before you enter.

lines.text: Imagine you buy BTC, and the price starts to fall. When do you get out?
lines.say: Imagine you buy B-T-C, and the price starts to fall. When do you get out?

lines.text: Deciding in the moment, under stress, is hard. Many beginners freeze, and the loss grows.
lines.say: Deciding in the moment, under stress, is hard. Many beginners freeze, and the loss grows.

lines.text: So plan both exits before you enter.
lines.say: So plan both exits before you enter.

lines.text: A trade plan has three prices: where you enter, where you get out if wrong, and where you take profit.
lines.say: A trade plan has three prices: where you enter, where you get out if wrong, and where you take profit.

lines.text: Entry 60,000. Stop-loss 59,400, below. Take-profit 61,200, above.
lines.say: Entry sixty thousand. Stop-loss fifty-nine thousand four hundred, below. Take-profit sixty-one thousand two hundred, above.

lines.text: For a short, it flips: the stop-loss goes above, the take-profit below.
lines.say: For a short, it flips: the stop-loss goes above, the take-profit below.

lines.text: A stop-loss is an order that closes your position if price moves against you, to limit the loss.
lines.say: A stop-loss is an order that closes your position if price moves against you, to limit the loss.

lines.text: Like a seat belt: it reduces the harm, but it can't prevent the crash.
lines.say: Like a seat belt: it reduces the harm, but it can't prevent the crash.

lines.text: Long 0.01 BTC at 60,000, stop at 59,400: loss about 600 × 0.01 = 6 USDT, before fees.
lines.say: Long zero point zero one B-T-C at sixty thousand, stop at fifty-nine thousand four hundred: loss about six hundred times zero point zero one equals six U-S-D-T, before fees.

lines.text: A take-profit closes your position when price reaches your target, to lock in a gain.
lines.say: A take-profit closes your position when price reaches your target, to lock in a gain.

lines.text: Like getting off the bus at the stop you planned, not riding on and hoping.
lines.say: Like getting off the bus at the stop you planned, not riding on and hoping.

lines.text: Take-profit at 61,200: gain about 1,200 × 0.01 = 12 USDT, before fees.
lines.say: Take-profit at sixty-one thousand two hundred: gain about one thousand two hundred times zero point zero one equals twelve U-S-D-T, before fees.

lines.text: Two prices matter. The trigger price starts the exit. The execution price is where it actually fills.
lines.say: Two prices matter. The trigger price starts the exit. The execution price is where it actually fills.

lines.text: Stop trigger 59,400. In a quick move, it fills at 59,380.
lines.say: Stop trigger fifty-nine thousand four hundred. In a quick move, it fills at fifty-nine thousand three hundred eighty.

lines.text: Loss: (59,380 − 60,000) × 0.01 = −6.20 USDT. A little worse than planned.
lines.say: Loss: (fifty-nine thousand three hundred eighty minus sixty thousand) times zero point zero one equals minus six point two U-S-D-T. A little worse than planned.

lines.text: The risk/reward ratio compares what you could lose with what you could gain.
lines.say: The risk-to-reward ratio compares what you could lose with what you could gain.

lines.text: Risk: 600 per BTC, or 6 USDT. Reward: 1,200 per BTC, or 12 USDT.
lines.say: Risk: six hundred per B-T-C, or six U-S-D-T. Reward: one thousand two hundred per B-T-C, or twelve U-S-D-T.

lines.text: 12 divided by 6 is 2. So this plan is 1 to 2: you risk 1 to aim for 2.
lines.say: Twelve divided by six is two. So this plan is one to two: you risk one to aim for two.

lines.text: All before fees. And it says nothing about how likely a win is.
lines.say: All before fees. And it says nothing about how likely a win is.

lines.text: Scenario one: price rises to 61,200. The take-profit triggers and fills.
lines.say: Scenario one: price rises to sixty-one thousand two hundred. The take-profit triggers and fills.

lines.text: Result: about plus 12 USDT before fees. The trade is closed.
lines.say: Result: about plus twelve U-S-D-T before fees. The trade is closed.

lines.text: On many platforms, when one exit fills, the other is cancelled. Check yours.
lines.say: On many platforms, when one exit fills, the other is cancelled. Check yours.

lines.text: Scenario two: price falls. The stop-loss triggers at 59,400 and fills at 59,390.
lines.say: Scenario two: price falls. The stop-loss triggers at fifty-nine thousand four hundred and fills at fifty-nine thousand three hundred ninety.

lines.text: Result: about minus 6.10 USDT before fees. A small, planned loss.
lines.say: Result: about minus six point one U-S-D-T before fees. A small, planned loss.

lines.text: Losing trades are normal. The stop kept this one small.
lines.say: Losing trades are normal. The stop kept this one small.

lines.text: Scenario three: bad news, and price gaps from 59,700 straight to 59,100.
lines.say: Scenario three: bad news, and price gaps from fifty-nine thousand seven hundred straight to fifty-nine thousand one hundred.

lines.text: The stop triggers, but the first available price is 59,100.
lines.say: The stop triggers, but the first available price is fifty-nine thousand one hundred.

lines.text: Loss: about 9 USDT, not the 6 you planned. Triggered is not the same as filled at your price.
lines.say: Loss: about nine U-S-D-T, not the six you planned. Triggered is not the same as filled at your price.

lines.text: A take-profit can also stay unfilled. Price reaches 61,150, just short of your 61,200.
lines.say: A take-profit can also stay unfilled. Price reaches sixty-one thousand one hundred fifty, just short of your sixty-one thousand two hundred.

lines.text: Then it turns down. No profit was taken, and the gain on screen shrinks.
lines.say: Then it turns down. No profit was taken, and the gain on screen shrinks.

lines.text: Unrealized profit is not money in hand until the position is closed.
lines.say: Unrealized profit is not money in hand until the position is closed.

lines.text: A common mistake: thinking a 1 to 2 plan means you will probably win.
lines.say: A common mistake: thinking a one to two plan means you will probably win.

lines.text: Risk/reward is about size, not chance. A plan can be 1 to 3 and still lose most of the time.
lines.say: Risk-to-reward is about size, not chance. A plan can be one to three and still lose most of the time.

lines.text: Judge the setup separately, and keep WAIT as an option.
lines.say: Judge the setup separately, and keep wait as an option.

lines.text: Your turn. Long 0.01 BTC at 60,000. Stop-loss 59,500. Take-profit 61,000.
lines.say: Your turn. Long zero point zero one B-T-C at sixty thousand. Stop-loss fifty-nine thousand five hundred. Take-profit sixty-one thousand.

lines.text: Work out the risk, the reward, and the ratio, before fees. Pause if you need to.
lines.say: Work out the risk, the reward, and the ratio, before fees. Pause if you need to.

lines.text: Risk: 500 × 0.01 = 5 USDT. Reward: 1,000 × 0.01 = 10 USDT.
lines.say: Risk: five hundred times zero point zero one equals five U-S-D-T. Reward: one thousand times zero point zero one equals ten U-S-D-T.

lines.text: So it is 1 to 2, before fees. Did you get it?
lines.say: So it is one to two, before fees. Did you get it?

lines.text: Stop-loss and take-profit help, but they have limits.
lines.say: Stop-loss and take-profit help, but they have limits.

lines.text: Stops can slip in fast moves, and take-profits may not fill.
lines.say: Stops can slip in fast moves, and take-profits may not fill.

lines.text: In futures with leverage (T12), the exchange can force-close a losing position. That is liquidation.
lines.say: In futures with leverage (T twelve), the exchange can force-close a losing position. That is liquidation.

lines.text: If you can't decide where your stop goes, that's a sign to wait.
lines.say: If you can't decide where your stop goes, that's a sign to wait.

lines.text: Let's recap.
lines.say: Let's recap.

lines.text: Plan entry, stop-loss and take-profit before you enter.
lines.say: Plan entry, stop-loss and take-profit before you enter.

lines.text: Trigger is not execution: stops can slip, and targets can be missed.
lines.say: Trigger is not execution: stops can slip, and targets can be missed.

lines.text: Risk/reward compares sizes, not chances.
lines.say: Risk-to-reward compares sizes, not chances.

lines.text: Check yourself: risk 8 USDT, reward 12 USDT. What's the ratio?
lines.say: Check yourself: risk eight U-S-D-T, reward twelve U-S-D-T. What's the ratio?

lines.text: 1 to 1.5: 12 divided by 8.
lines.say: One to one point five: twelve divided by eight.

lines.text: Well done! Next up, T09: fees, spread and slippage, the costs that eat small wins.
lines.say: Well done! Next up, T nine: fees, spread and slippage, the costs that eat small wins.
